question: Which gas is evolved when a metal reacts with a dilute acid?
solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a **reactive metal** reacts with a **dilute acid**, it typically produces a **metal salt** and evolves **Hydrogen gas**.
 
• The general chemical equation for this reaction is: **Metal + Dilute Acid → Metal Salt + Hydrogen (H2)**.
 
• This process is classified as a **displacement reaction** because the metal atoms displace **hydrogen atoms** from the acid molecules. ***Hence, the correct answer is Hydrogen.***
 
• For example, when **Zinc (Zn)** granules are added to **dilute Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, the reaction yields **Zinc Chloride (ZnCl2)** and releases **Hydrogen gas**.
 
• Not all metals react with dilute acids; only those metals that are placed **above hydrogen** in the **reactivity series** (like **Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc,** and **Iron**) can displace it.
